newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden sees pre-New Year air cargo rush to China.
newsitem.headline: Sweden sees pre-New Year air cargo rush to China.

text.p: Several charters flew to China from Sweden to handle a surge of air cargo volumes ahead of an increase in import fees into China which took effect on January 1, freight forwarders said on Thursday.

Although they were unable to say exactly how many aircraft outside regularly scheduled traffic flew from the area, players said alternatives had to be brought in to meet a rise in shipments ahead of the new year.
"The situation was completely crazy for the mainland China business," said Berry Christiansson, managing director of freight forwarder Air Consultants, based in Malmo, Sweden.
"Everyone wanted to have customs clearance by January 1," he told Reuters."
The company chartered an Ilyushin Il-76 with a capacity of 40 tonnes from Stockholm to Tianjin for Finnish machinery, Christiansson said.
"There must have been four to five charters from the Stockholm area," he added.
Joanna Falk, in the export division of freight forwarders Penta Shipping Aircargo AB, said the new import regulations in China would mean higher prices.
"The only thing I know is that it will be more expensive -- about 30 percent," she told Reuters.
Three or four Boeing-747 Combi versions with a capacity of around 100 tonnes were chartered through Penta, Falk said.
She added, however, that this was usual for December.
"It's like this every year," she said.

Jan Wallin, of freight forwarder Panalpina, said the company had used its Boeing-747 freighter which operates from Skavsta airport once weekly in addition to a charter flight on December 26 to Guangzhou via Beijing with 90 tonnes of cargo.
"We have been using every possible way out," he said.
Swedish telecommunication firm LM Ericsson AB's public telecom division sent some 400 tonnes through Panalpina in December, Wallin said.
"The contract stipulated delivery by January 1," he said.
Wallin said there had been significant blocked space shipments as well.

Freight forwarder ASG Air & Sea AB chartered several aircraft for Ericsson's mobile telephone division, an ASG spokesman told Reuters. He declined to give any more information about the chartered flights.
No one at Ericsson was available for comment.
